1: # Team evals
2: 
3: An eval is your own world for the challenge: a web app with up to four sites, a task and its one correct answer. The
4: platform hosts it and runs agents on it, yours or, once you make it public, every team's, each on its own
5: leaderboard. Use it to test your agent on cases the public scenario doesn't have.
6: 
7: ## Quickstart
8: 
9: ```sh
10: atira eval init my-eval          # the starter kit: four sites, a bid configurator, BRIEF.md, expected.json
11: atira eval dev my-eval           # run it here; each answer is scored against expected.json and printed
12: atira eval deploy my-eval        # upload it: streams the build, then prints the world's URLs and preview logins
13: atira eval run my-eval --package submission --repeats 3
14: atira eval runs my-eval          # mean quality ± sd over the repeats, mean cost and time
15: atira eval deploy my-eval --public   # every team can run on it; it gets a leaderboard
16: ```
17: 
18: The starter kit is a working eval: four basic sites like the challenge's (tender portal, customer portal, ERP and
19: mail), a brief and the expected bid. They're deliberately far too simple. Make yours harder, then deploy.
20: 
21: `atira eval dev` starts your app on `127.0.0.1:8710` (8711–8713 for the next sites) with the platform's environment,
22: `ATIRA_API_URL` pointing at a local stand-in for the platform's two endpoints, and prints a login per site. Open the
23: URLs in a browser and sign in, or run your agent against them: in another terminal,
24: `eval "$(atira eval dev --env my-eval)"` exports the run as `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` with the logins, the way
25: `atira scout --env` does, so an agent built on the starter kit runs unchanged. Every answer your app hands in is
26: scored against `expected.json` and printed. Change the app, restart `dev`, try again: nothing is uploaded.
27: 
28: The first `deploy` creates the eval, private, and remembers its id in `my-eval/.atira/eval.json`; every later deploy
29: pushes a new version. Past runs stay with the version they ran on. In an eval's folder, `<eval>` can be left out of
30: the other commands; elsewhere give its id (`ev_...`) or slug. Your coding agent gets them as tools through
31: [`atira mcp`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md): `eval_init`, `eval_dev`, `eval_deploy`, `eval_preview`, `eval_run`, `eval_runs` and
32: `eval_board`, `eval_list`, `eval_status` and `eval_source`.

34: Other commands: `atira eval ls` lists your evals and the public ones, `atira eval status` shows the versions and the

38: ## The bundle
39: 
40: The folder you deploy, with `.gitignore` respected (`.git`, `node_modules` and `.atira` always stay out), at most
41: 50 MB compressed. At its root:
42: 
43: - `atira-eval.json`, the manifest:
44: 
45:   ```json
46:   { "build": "npm ci", "start": "node server.js", "sites": [{ "name": "portal", "port": 3000 }] }
47:   ```
48: 
49:   - `build` (optional) runs once when the version is built; `start` starts every site. Both are shell commands run in
50:     the bundle's folder.
51:   - `sites`: 1–4 sites, each a `name` (a–z, 0–9 and `-`, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters) and the

53:   - `world` (optional) may only be `"shared"`: every eval has one VM, its current version's, for every run and

56: - `expected.json`: the correct answer, in the challenge's answer schema (the RFQ bid: `atira challenge rfq` shows it).

58: See [the world and its contract](#the-world-and-its-contract) for what your app reads and calls.

90: ## The world and its contract
91: 
92: Each version runs in **one permanent VM, its world**, from the moment its build is ready. Agents and you open its sites
93: directly on their public URLs; there is no gateway in front. Your app signs agents in and hands their answer in
94: itself, through two platform endpoints, the way the challenge's own sites do. The starter kit's `atira-kit.js` does
95: both: copy it into your app.
96: 
97: The app starts with, `<NAME>` being the site's name upper-cased with `_` for `-`:
98: 
99: | Variable | What |
100: | --- | --- |
101: | `PORT_<NAME>` | the port to listen on; use it rather than the manifest's |
102: | `ATIRA_SITE_URL_<NAME>` | the site's own public URL, for links between your sites |
103: | `ATIRA_API_URL` | the platform API's origin, the only host the world reaches |
104: | `ATIRA_EVAL_TOKEN` | a secret bearer for this version only |
105: 
106: Each run's agent gets a login per site (username `u_…`, a password), as on the challenge's sites; a preview's are
107: `p_…`. Both endpoints take `Authorization: Bearer $ATIRA_EVAL_TOKEN` and JSON:
108: 
109: - `POST $ATIRA_API_URL/v1/eval-worlds/verify` `{"site": "portal", "username": "u_…", "password": "…"}`: 200
110:   `{"run_id": "run_…", "expires_at": 1760001200000}` (`preview_id` for a preview), else 401. Keep the session in a
111:   signed cookie and ask again at most every 10 s, so an ended run is signed out.
112: - `POST $ATIRA_API_URL/v1/eval-worlds/answer` `{"run_id": "run_…", "bid": {…}}` (or `preview_id`): for a run `202`
113:   and the run ends; for a preview `200` `{"accepted": true, "score": {"quality", "eligible", "breakdown"}}` and you can
114:   submit again; `400` `{"issues": [{"path", "message"}]}` for a bid that fails the answer schema, so the page can show
115:   them and the agent can try again; `409` once the run has its answer.
116: 
117: `atira eval dev` serves both endpoints locally with the same paths, fields and env.
118: 
119: ### Next.js
120: 
121: Copy `atira-kit.js` next to your app (it is plain Node, ESM), then a sign-in route, a guard and an answer route:
122: 
123: ```ts
124: // app/login/route.ts: POST username, password (and returnTo) from your login page's form
125: import { signIn } from "@/atira-kit.js"
126: export async function POST(request: Request) {
127:   const form = await request.formData()
128:   const signed = await signIn("web", String(form.get("username")), String(form.get("password")), true)
129:   if (!signed) return Response.redirect(new URL("/login?error=1", request.url), 303)
130:   return new Response(null, { status: 303, headers: { location: "/", "set-cookie": signed.cookie } })
131: }
132: 
133: // in a server component or route handler: the login, or off to /login
134: import { cookies } from "next/headers"
135: import { redirect } from "next/navigation"
136: import { currentLogin } from "@/atira-kit.js"
137: const login = await currentLogin((await cookies()).toString(), "web")
138: if (!login) redirect("/login")
139: 
140: // app/answer/route.ts: the browser POSTs the bid here; the app hands it to the platform
141: import { currentLogin, submitAnswer } from "@/atira-kit.js"
142: export async function POST(request: Request) {
143:   const login = await currentLogin(request.headers.get("cookie"), "web")
144:   if (!login) return Response.json({ error: "Bitte anmelden." }, { status: 401 })
145:   const { status, body } = await submitAnswer(login, await request.json())
146:   return Response.json(body, { status })
147: }
148: ```
149: 
150: Run it on the Node.js runtime (the default), not the Edge runtime: the kit uses `node:crypto`. With Express,
151: `guard(req, res, "web")` from the kit serves `/login` and `/logout` and returns the login (or null once it has
152: answered), as the starter kit's `server.js` does.
153: 
154: ## The answer
155: 
156: It is scored with the main challenge's scorer, against your `expected.json`: the decision must match; then the tender
157: reference 5 points, the discount 5, the net total 15 (it must also be the sum of the lines) and 75 for the positions,
158: shared equally, each split into material 35 %, quantity 20 %, unit price 30 % and lead time 15 %. A line for a
159: position your answer doesn't have costs one position's share. Breakdown fields such as `base_unit_price` are
160: accepted and not scored.
161: 
162: ## Runs, previews and leaderboards
163: 
164: - `atira eval preview` gives you logins per site on the eval's one world for a few hours (`--hours`, 1–8), at once;
165:   nothing boots for it, and the world is never restarted on request. A bid you submit there is scored against
166:   `expected.json`.
167: - `atira eval run` runs a package: your latest submission's (`--package submission`, the default), your latest test
168:   run's (`test`), any earlier submission's or run's of your team by its id (`--package sub_...` or `run_...`, scored or
169:   not, as long as its package is still stored), or a folder (`--package ./my-agent`), 1–3 times (`--repeats`). Name an
170:   entry with `--label`, or later with `atira run name <run> "name"` (only your team sees names). Each run is an ordinary run: its page,
171:   logs, screenshots and `diagnose_run` work as for test runs, with the scored run's 20-minute limit.
172: - Private evals (the default) are yours alone, their runs too: a run's page and logs answer 404 to anyone outside your
173:   team. Public ones: any team runs on them and reads their source, `expected.json`
174:   included. Each version has its own leaderboard (`atira eval board`): each team's best entry, by mean quality, then
175:   cost × time.
176: 
177: Limits, unless the organizers change them: 10 evals a team and 12 eval runs an hour (each repeat counts), and
178: previews for up to 8 hours. Eval runs share your team's test-run limit: up to 12 test and eval
179: runs at a time and 12 waiting, together.
180: 
181: ## Security
182: 
183: - The world reaches only the platform's API (`ATIRA_API_URL`): everything else it needs is in the bundle or made by
184:   `build`.
185: - Every page should need a login: the sites are on public URLs. The starter kit's `atira-kit.js` does it, verifying
186:   each login with the platform.

188:   the environment, never from the bundle.
189: - A private eval's sites get unguessable URLs; a public eval's are named after its slug.
190: - One world serves every run of the version: keep each run's state apart (by its run id).
